_purpose: what the step-2 regression test (new engine vs these goldens) compares and at what tolerance

captured_under.note: manifest.json carries the full interpreter string, openpyxl and scipy versions and the git revisions of both repos; goldens are LF-terminated JSON

tolerance.rule: numeric leaf passes when |new-golden| <= atol + rtol*max(|new|,|golden|)
tolerance.why_atol: leaves that are zero up to rounding (compare_fitting_methods 'Mean % error' for MUPE/ZMPE rows ~1e-16, 'Bias', cfg.SingularTol) cannot be compared relatively

authority_1e-9.rule: these leaves are never rounded by the engine; they are compared at rtol 1e-9 (+ atol 1e-12) and are the authority whenever a rounded or derived leaf moves
leaves: engine_*.json / engine_*.lib.json ctx: t1_lc, t1_rt, t1_br, b_lc, b_rt, b_br, c_br, rate_sd, fit_c, fit_q, fit_se, n_keep, n_unit, rate_ok, rate_why, mdl_lc / mdl_rt / mdl_lcr Beta, SE, Fitted, SSE, InvDiag, R2, AdjR2, SEy, F, DF, SSreg, SSresid, N, K, Converged (Iter / Delta live in iteration_detail); ctx.cfg exact
derived_stats (sst_log and per model SEE, R2, AdjR2, CV, MAPE, Bias, AICc, t_rate, se_rate, t_all, dAICc)

midpoints.analogy_midpoints_<model> and midpoints.forecast_unrounded.<model> midpoint / unit_cost / lot_cost_before / lot_cost_after (recomputed with the module's own lmp_func; rounding them to 4 / 2 dp reproduces the projections columns exactly)
intervals 'SE (log)' and 'Level' in every interval frame
enrich.<model>.influence_diagnostics and wbs influence_table: 'Actual ($K)', 'Fitted ($K)', '% error', 'Leverage', "Cook's D", 'DFFITS'

enrich.<model>.compare_fitting_methods: OLS row, log_residual_variance, theoretical_factor, smearing_factor, mupe_over_ols, zmpe_over_ols, percent_understated (MUPE / ZMPE rows: see expected_to_move_beyond_rtol_in_step_2)

lots_cost_core.json fit.t1 / b / c / slope / rate_slope / sigma / cv / r_squared / ctx / derived_stats / equation_detail numbers; per_lot fitted_unit_cost / fitted_lot_cost / residual / percent_error (LotFitReport._fitted rebuilds them from ctx at full precision, lots.py:847-858, NOT from the 4-dp lot_midpoint column); learning_curve_compare_methods.*.fits (theta, cov, sigma, fitted, mean_percent_error, standard_error, cv, r_squared)
wbs_*.json elements[].ctx and elements[].derived_stats (also inside overrides.* and wbs_extra_programs)
cli_fit_lots.json csv_contents (the CSVs are written at full repr precision, parsed round_trip) and csv_text / sha256
error_paths.json texts and app_run_file.json fields (exact equality)

rounded_leaves.rule: for the columns listed in atol_by_column (dp = decimals the engine rounds to): a leaf passes when |new-golden| <= half_unit + rtol*|golden| (= 0.5*10^-dp, the rounding half-width) if the NEW side is the unrounded value, and when |new-golden| <= one_unit * (1 + 1e-6) + atol (= 10^-dp) if both sides are rounded, because a value within 1e-9 of a half-unit boundary flips by exactly one unit in the last place. A leaf that moves by more than one unit is a real regression. Sums of rounded leaves (sums_of_rounded) get n_terms * one_unit. The unrounded counterparts in authority_1e-9 stay under the 1e-9 rule and decide a flip
sums_of_rounded: engine projections_column_sums[<rounded column>]: n_rows units of that column

wbs elements[].total and elements[].by_lot of fitted elements (wbs.py:506-519 sum the 2-dp '<model> Lot Cost After Complexity ($)' column), deterministic.total, simulated_run_point_total, overrides.*.ok.total and .elements[].total (wbs.py:614), wbs_extra_programs programs.*.deterministic.*: n_terms x 0.01
risk_run_risk.total_point / risk_variants.*.total_point (risk.py:199, sum of the 2-dp 'Lot Cost ($)'): n_lots x 0.01

enrich simulate_buy point_estimate (enrich.py:520, 558: sum of the 2-dp lot costs) in every simulate_buy block, enrich_run_*.risk, test_lotmodel_fixtures.*, element_standalone_simulate_buy, lots simulate.*: n_lots x 0.01
wbs by_fiscal_year 'Total ($)' / 'Cumulative ($)' (sums of 2-dp values, re-rounded): n_terms x 0.01

derived_from_rounded.rule: compared at rtol 1e-9 (they are deterministic and seeded). When one fails, the step-2 comparator must find a one-unit flip in the base leaf named here, and the derived leaf must have moved by the same FACTOR (products) or the same ABSOLUTE amount (sums) as that base; any other move is a real regression. These are therefore not authority leaves: the authority for what they encode is authority_1e-9 (ctx / derived_stats / midpoints.forecast_unrounded / 'SE (log)')
derived_from_rounded.simulate_buy totals_first_10 / totals_su: rounded lot costs x seeded lognormal draws (enrich.py:507-558)
derived_from_rounded.risk_run_risk / risk_variants.* / test_w: the same draws (risk.py:230-257); the S-curve is additionally rounded to 2 dp
derived_from_rounded.wbs element_standalone_simulate_buy.*, p: the same draws on the elements' 2-dp lot costs (program_level_percentiles is also step-3 rebaselined)
derived_from_rounded.wbs factor / amount elements' by_lot and: factor x the rounded bases (wbs.py:452) / the amounts as given (wbs.py:433)
derived_from_rounded.test_workbook_fixture.scurve_markers E2_: the P50 / P80 of the same draws

rounded_leaves.formatted_strings: summary/model_comparison/Risk_Summary/program_summary values are formatted strings (lot_cost_model.py:1136-1250, risk.py:255-300, wbs.py:853-916) compared for exact equality; a last-printed-digit flip is judged against derived_stats, not failed outright

missing_values_in_frames.rule: inside DataFrame record leaves (the 'records' lists), null, "nan" and "NA" are all a missing value and compare equal; inside ctx scalars and every other leaf None-vs-NaN is a real regression and is reported
missing_values_in_frames.why: captured on pandas 3.0.3, where text columns carry dtype 'str' and a missing text value comes back from .tolist() as float nan -> "nan" (golden dtypes show 'Lot': 'str'); verified on the scratch Python 3.9 venv with pandas 2.3.3 / numpy 2.0.2 that the same frame is object dtype and a None stays None -> null, and that a pandas 'string' column yields pd.NA -> "NA"

exclude_from_step2._note: minimal and permanent (they apply to step 2 and every later step): nothing the engine computes is excluded; every item is provenance, a loop counter, a documented app/lib config difference, or a path / informational field
items: provenance rows 'Tool version' and 'Run timestamp' (already stripped into provenance.nongolden.json)

engine_*.json: iteration_detail (Iter/Delta of the midpoint loop; Converged stays in ctx) EXCEPT for cases app_example_maxiter_1, app_example_maxiter_2, app_example_tol_1e-14 where Iter, Delta, Converged and fit_status are golden
engine_*.json: ctx.cfg.ToolVersion (app None vs lib '2.0-dev'); *.dtypes blocks are informational
engine_*.json: ctx.cfg is the settings dict (inputs, e.g. SingularTol 1e-12, Tol 1e-9): compare it for exact equality, not with the atol rule, so a changed default is caught
cli_fit_lots.json: 'Source:' in assumptions_md and cmd[--csv] are relative to the library root by design; stdout_lines are informational; assumptions_md text is compared (timestamp already stripped)
app_run_file.json: saved_at and tool_version are already stripped; output_path is masked
error_paths.json: compare the error TEXT for the substring each test asserts (listed in the test line references); the full text is pinned so a rewording is visible, not so it is forbidden
capture_warnings / *.warnings lists: informational (expected_to_move_beyond_rtol_in_step_2 names the one that may change)

exclude_after_step3._note: nothing is excluded here any more. This entry used to name the blocks step 3 was allowed to stop comparing; step 3 rebaselined them to their new values instead, so they are still compared leaf by leaf at the general rule and this entry is the record of what moved. golden_support._EXCLUDE_AFTER_STEP3 is empty to match, and tests/test_goldens.py GOLDEN_STAGE stays at 2
exclude_after_step3._what_was_rebaselined: the program_level_percentiles block of tests/goldens/wbs_TEST_PROGRAM.json.gz and tests/goldens/wbs_FULL_WBS.json.gz, and nothing else in either file. wbs_extra_programs.json.gz carries no such block and was not touched; its programmes are captured with simulate=False
exclude_after_step3._when: 2026-09-07, with the commit that replaced the lognormal handoff in cost_core/program/rollup.py with the empirical marginal in cost_core/monte_carlo.py
exclude_after_step3._why: each fitted element used to reach the risk model as a two-parameter lognormal fitted to its own simulated buy totals, because RiskModel took distributions and not draws. An element total is a sum of correlated lognormal lot costs and is not itself lognormal, so that summary ran high through the working range: measured against the element's own percentiles it was 0.79% to 1.23% out at its worst level, and 0 of 99 levels agreed. The draws now go through unchanged, so all 99 agree exactly. The programme percentiles move because the summary they replace was wrong, not because the simulation became noisier
exclude_after_step3._how: the block was regenerated by golden_support.capture_wbs on the programme rebuilt from the golden's own inputs, spliced into the existing file, and written back through the same path the capture used (json.dumps indent=1, gzip level 9 with mtime 0). That path was proved byte-identical on all 42 goldens before either file was opened for writing, and every block outside program_level_percentiles was compared afterwards and is unchanged on disk
exclude_after_step3._leaves_that_moved: 162 in wbs_TEST_PROGRAM and 186 in wbs_FULL_WBS, every one of them inside program_level_percentiles and one of each being the block's own _note. The count is the measurement: the comparator was run over a fresh capture against the old file and reported nothing outside the block. Two further leaves in FULL_WBS moved within a rounded-column allowance and so are not in the comparator's count

reserve_to_p80._what: p80 minus the deterministic point total: the risk reserve a budget would have to carry to reach the 80th percentile

p99._what: read off the S-curve, which is rounded to cents

exclude_after_step3._second_effect: the programme standard deviation falls 1.02% even though the element variances rise about 4%. A Gaussian copula attenuates a heavier-tailed marginal more, so the achieved Pearson correlation between the three fitted elements drops from a mean of 0.262 to 0.216 while Spearman does not move; pair by pair, 0.279, 0.241 and 0.267 become 0.225, 0.189 and 0.235. Variance rose, covariance fell further, and the total narrowed. That is also why independence_understates_sd_by falls further than variance_ratio_analytic, which is computed from the marginal variances and the requested correlation rather than from the sample. On the standard deviation scale that test_the_sampler_agrees_with_the_algebra_on_correlation compares, the disagreement between the two went from 0.07% to 3.14%, leaving 1.86 of the 5 percentage points allowed where 4.93 were left before
wbs_<program>.xlsx: the risk rows/columns of Program_Summary and Program_Elements. compare_workbooks.py --skip-sheets cannot skip rows, so the _plain / _plain_nosens variants are the ones to regress at 1e-9; the risk variant moved with the block above
exclude_after_step3.not_affected_by_step_3: element_standalone_simulate_buy (per-element simulate_buy at 8000/11/0.30), simulated_run_point_total, and every engine_*.json simulate/risk block. All three were checked and are byte-identical: the element draws did not move, only what the programme does with them. The block's warnings leaf did not move either, although the old exclusion list named it

expected_to_move_beyond_rtol_in_step_2._what: the MUPE and ZMPE rows of every compare_fitting_methods frame, once the private _fit_mupe / _fit_zmpe in enrich.py are replaced by cost_core.fitting.fit_all_methods. tests/golden_support.py builds its OVERRIDES table from this entry, so the two cannot disagree about the size of the carve-out
expected_to_move_beyond_rtol_in_step_2._why: the two estimators are iterative and they stop on different rules. fitting's MUPE stops on its inner least-squares step and enrich's stopped on the parameter step; fitting's ZMPE seeds Nelder-Mead from the MUPE solution and enrich's seeded it from OLS. Neither is more nearly right than the other, they are different fixed points of the same objective, so the gap does not close by tightening a tolerance
expected_to_move_beyond_rtol_in_step_2._measured_not_guessed: measured on the whole golden corpus (36 engine cases, the lots family, the two WBS programmes and the three CLI runs) by re-running the comparator with the carve-out switched off and recording every leaf that then disagrees. _measured_maxima below is that measurement, so a later step can re-run it and see whether the corpus still moves by what this entry says it does. It was taken on both supported lanes, python 3.14 with numpy 2.4.4 and pandas 3.0.3 and python 3.9 with numpy 2.0.2 and pandas 2.3.3, and the two agree to four digits on every figure. The step-2 prototype had measured the 36 engine cases alone and sized the coefficients at 1e-6 relative and Mean % error at 1e-11 absolute; one of those two sizes survived the full measurement and the other did not, and _sizes_the_prototype_proposed says which and why. The ZMPE row was never reproducible better than about 1e-7 even against itself from seed perturbation alone, which is why the coefficient allowance is 1e-6 and not 1e-8
expected_to_move_beyond_rtol_in_step_2._how_the_allowances_are_sized: pulled from two directions. From below, an allowance has to admit the largest move measured with room to spare, or a rerun on another BLAS or numpy build lands on the line. From above, it has to stay under the resolution the number is published at, which for this table is four significant figures (AssumptionLog.table's ',.4g' float format, cost_core/reporting/assumptions.py:86), or a move an analyst could read passes unseen. The rule the two directions come out to is one line: the smallest power of ten that clears the measured maximum by at least three times. Column by column that is T1 1e-6 over 1.582e-7 (6.3x), c (rate) 1e-6 over 3.295e-7 (3.0x), MAPE 1e-6 over 3.319e-7 (3.0x), SEE (log) 1e-7 over 5.924e-9 (16.9x), Mean % error 1e-8 over 6.905e-10 (14.5x), the b (learning) atol 1e-7 over the 5.347e-9 the one leaf that needs it moves (18.7x) and derived_stats Bias 1e-10 over 4.058e-12 (24.6x). MAPE and c (rate) sit at the three-times floor because the next power of ten up would put the allowance at the fourth significant figure itself and buy headroom by giving up the ability to see anything. Most allowances are two orders of magnitude below what is printed; the b atol is one. b (learning) is also the one column whose relative allowance does not carry its column on its own, which _atol_on_the_exponents says out loud rather than leaving to be discovered. Every number the sizing rests on is in _measured_maxima
expected_to_move_beyond_rtol_in_step_2._sizes_the_prototype_proposed: the step-2 prototype proposed 1e-6 relative on T1, the exponents and MAPE, 1e-8 relative on SEE (log) and 1e-11 absolute on Mean % error. The first survived measurement unchanged. The other two are recorded here because a later step reading the step-2 brief would otherwise find them and take the shipped numbers for a carve-out widened without measurement. Mean % error at 1e-11 does not admit the corpus at all, and what it fails on is not the lots family but the engine cases the prototype itself had in front of it: the MUPE row moves 6.905e-10 on engine rate_driven_8lots and 1.008e-11 on engine app_example_maxiter_2, because the golden value there is a cancelling sum of order 1e-16 and the new one is the same sum computed by a different estimator. The prototype had sized that column from the coefficients rather than from the column itself. SEE (log) does fit under 1e-8, at 1.69x, which is tighter than every other column here and tighter than the three-times floor, so it is sized at 1e-7 by the same rule as the rest rather than left as the one column with no room to rerun on another BLAS

_measured_maxima._note: the largest move each carved-out column actually makes, re-measured after the exact-fit gate went into summary.py and on both supported lanes, which agree on every figure here to four digits. leaves_needing_atol counts the leaves whose relative move exceeds the rtol, which is the only thing an absolute allowance has to cover; atol_needed is the largest absolute move among those. A column with none does not carry an atol. Two entries record a rel far above one: Mean % error and derived_stats Bias are cancelling sums whose golden value sits at the floating-point floor, so the relative move on them is arithmetic about nothing and only the absolute one is sized

expected_to_move_beyond_rtol_in_step_2.seeded_risk_draws: the seeded simulate_buy totals are NOT bit-identical to the goldens and cannot be, which is worth writing down because it is easy to ask for the wrong thing here. A draw is beta + L z with z from a seeded generator: the generator, the Cholesky and the arithmetic are unchanged, so z is bit-identical, but beta moved in the 13th digit and so the totals move with it, by up to 9.4e-11 relative (four_lots LC+Rate std). That is inside the general rtol 1e-9 and no allowance is taken for it. The property that IS bit-identity, and that was checked: feeding ede4a29's own beta, cov and sigma into the new simulate_buy reproduces the old totals exactly on all 102 fits in the corpus, and the 33 pure Rate fits, whose design does not depend on b and whose beta therefore did not move, reproduce the golden totals exactly as they stand. Step 3 should ask for that property, not for bit-identical totals
expected_to_move_beyond_rtol_in_step_2.unchanged_at_the_general_rule: everything else in those blocks stays at rtol 1e-9 / atol 1e-12: the OLS row of the same frames, log_residual_variance, theoretical_factor, smearing_factor, percent_understated, mupe_over_ols and zmpe_over_ols. A move in any of those is a real regression, because they are computed from the OLS fit that the engine itself reports

also_changed_in_step_2.DFFITS: cost_core/cer/diagnostics.py now reports DFFITS as 0.0 when the fit has fewer than two degrees of freedom. It is a change to the CER package's shared compute_diagnostics and so reaches every caller at that many degrees of freedom, not only the lot engine. The leave-one-out residual scale is 0/0 there, so the published value was a ratio of rounding errors: perturbing the design by 1e-13 flips it by order one while every other diagnostic stays put. Thirteen golden leaves are affected, all of them in df == 1 fits; dffits_below_two_df.affected lists them by case, counted by switching the allowance off and running the suite. They are accepted as 0.0 by that rule rather than rebaselined, which keeps the old values on the record. DFFITS is listed in authority_1e-9, which is why the change is noted here
also_changed_in_step_2.engine_app_example_tol_1e-14: the LC+Rate iteration_detail Iter and Delta, ctx.mdl_lcr.Converged and fit_status of that one case were rebaselined; see tests/goldens/README.md for the old and new values and why the old one was an artefact of solver error
also_changed_in_step_2.rate_t_on_an_exact_fit: cost_core/lotmodel/summary.py now reports the rate t-statistic as not available when the fit's residual scale is at the floating-point floor, so model selection cannot turn on the ratio of two rounding errors. The test is sigma <= 1e-10 * max(|fitted|) on the fitting scale, which is the test cost_core/cer/diagnostics.py already applies before dividing by that scale. It is not a close call anywhere: instrumenting all 17953 lot fits the test suite performs, the ratio is either at or below 1.1e-14 (14 fits, every one of them inside the two exact-fit lots fixtures) or at or above 2.6e-4, so nothing in the corpus is within six orders of magnitude of the threshold in either direction. It changes one printed cell in each of the two fixtures, t (rate coefficient), from 0.93 and 0.11 to n/a, and it is what keeps them selecting LC. The selection note beside it still reads 'Rate coefficient not significant (|t| < 2.0)', which is the wording the golden already carried and the reason it is not on any exclusion list; on an exact fit the more exact sentence would be that there was no scale to test against, but that is a change to a published string and it is not this step's to make. tests/test_lotmodel.py::test_the_rate_t_is_withheld_when_there_is_no_residual_scale_to_form_it pins both halves of the rule, the withholding on a series priced off the curve and the t still being formed on data that has a residual scale. See exact_fit_fixtures._what_it_does_not_cover

expected_to_move_beyond_rtol_in_step_2._atol_on_the_exponents: b (learning) carries an absolute allowance as well as a relative one because a learning exponent can sit at nearly zero on a flat series, where a relative comparison of two numbers that are both nearly nothing says nothing. Exactly one leaf in the corpus is like that, and it is the only leaf anywhere whose relative move exceeds its rtol: the ZMPE exponent of the reference series escalated back to flat at 4% is 0.0036265630 against 0.0036265683, which is 1.5e-6 relative and 5.3e-9 absolute. 1e-7 admits it with nineteen times to spare and is still ten times below the last of the four significant figures that exponent prints to. c (rate) carried an absolute allowance as well and no longer does: no leaf in the corpus needs one, and an allowance nothing takes is an allowance nobody has measured

derived_stats_Bias._why: derived_stats Bias is the mean percentage error of the OLS retransformation, which is a number of order 1e-5 built out of cancelling residuals. tolerance.why_atol already names it as a leaf that cannot be compared relatively, so the general 1e-12 does not apply to it. Nine leaves move, by at most 4.06e-12 absolute, the largest on engine_app_example_fit_prior_10 LC+Rate. 1e-10 admits that with twenty-four times to spare and is still six orders of magnitude below the +0.00% the summary prints Bias to. Everything else in derived_stats stays at the general rule

dffits_below_two_df._what: cost_core/cer/diagnostics.py now reports DFFITS as 0.0 when the fit has fewer than two degrees of freedom, and the goldens carry the old value there
dffits_below_two_df._where_the_change_lives: compute_diagnostics is the CER package's own public entry point, not a lot-model path, so the rule reaches every caller that hands it a fit with fewer than two degrees of freedom and not only the lot engine. The 13 affected leaves below are all lot fits, but that is a statement about what the goldens contain rather than about the scope of the change, and it is written down here so the next reader does not have to infer the blast radius from the list
dffits_below_two_df._why: DFFITS divides by the leave-one-out residual scale, and at one degree of freedom dropping the one spare observation leaves nothing to estimate a scale from. Numerator and denominator are both at the floating-point floor and the quotient is whatever the last bits happen to say: the golden values are 4.4e5 to 2.1e6, against a conventional flag of about 1. Perturbing the design by 1e-13 flips them by order one with the formula untouched, so they were never a statement about the fit. Reported as zero instead
dffits_below_two_df._scope: the allowance is only ever taken when the new value is exactly zero and the golden is larger than 1000, which no real DFFITS is. A DFFITS that merely moved would still fail
dffits_below_two_df.affected: 13 leaves, counted by switching the allowance off and running the suite: engine_three_lots (3, LC on 3 lots and 2 parameters), engine_four_lots (3, LC+Rate on 4 lots and 3 parameters), engine_runfile_qty_only_4lot (3, LC on 4 lots) and lots_cost_core (4, three in the labelled_csv report and one in the three_lots report). Each engine case contributes the same lot three times, once through influence_diagnostics and once through each of the two enrich_run sheets. No CLI leaf is affected: all three test_cli_fit_lots cases pass with the allowance switched off

exact_fit_fixtures._what: two lots fixtures are built by evaluating the learning curve exactly at each lot midpoint and feeding the result back in, so the fit passes through every point and the residual scale is at the floating-point floor: sigma is about 1e-14 of the fitted values
exact_fit_fixtures._why: everything derived from that residual scale is a ratio of rounding errors. The goldens record F = 1.8e26, t = 1.2e14 and the rate coefficient at 1.3e-12 with a standard error of the same size. The accurate estimator makes the residuals smaller still, which moves those ratios by whole factors: F goes from 1.8e26 to 3.8e26, AICc from -354.25 to -358.71, and the largest of six residuals that are all at the floating-point floor changes which lot it belongs to. None of it is a statement about the fit
exact_fit_fixtures._what_it_does_not_cover: which model the tool selects. Before the gate went into summary.py this carve-out was also hiding the rate t-statistic crossing the 2.0 threshold on these two fixtures, and with it selected_model, the printed equation, df, n_params, the selection note and the analyst narrative. Hiding a change in which model the tool recommends behind a comparator exclusion is not a tolerance decision, so the code was changed instead: cost_core/lotmodel/summary.py now reports the rate t as not available when the residual scale is at the floating-point floor, the same test cost_core/cer/diagnostics.py already applies before dividing by that scale. Both fixtures select LC as they always did, and selected_model, selection_note, equation, equation_detail, df, n_params, c, rate_slope, the report summary values, the influence leverages and the methods table's model are all compared here at the general rule
exact_fit_fixtures._leaves_note: the list is the measurement, not a guess: it is exactly the leaves that still disagree when the exclusion is switched off and the suite is run. Every one of them is F, a standard error, an AICc, a t-statistic or a residual, all of them built from a sigma of about 1e-14 relative. The narrative is on the list because its last sentence names the lot with the largest departure, and all six departures are zero to eleven decimals, so which one is largest is decided by the last bit; the number it prints is -0.0% either way
exact_fit_fixtures.still_compared: everything the analyst is actually given: the selected model and its equation, the lot midpoints, unit costs, lot costs, projections, intervals and the risk draws all stay under the general rule in these fixtures and none of them moved
exact_fit_fixtures._blocks_note: anchored with a lookahead so the block name has to be a whole path segment: clean_series_escalated_* is a different fixture, is not an exact fit, and is not carved out

printed_mupe_zmpe_rows._what: the markdown assumption log prints the same fit-method table, so its MUPE and ZMPE rows carry the carve-out above at four significant figures
printed_mupe_zmpe_rows._scope: the two table rows are dropped from both sides and every other line of the document is still compared byte for byte; the sha256 beside it hashes the unmasked text and is therefore not compared. The only lines that moved are those two, in all four documents

full_repr_csv_bytes._what: the CLI writes its CSVs at full repr precision, so their bytes carry the last digit of every coefficient. Step 2 moves the coefficients in the 13th digit, which changes those bytes and their sha256
full_repr_csv_bytes._why: byte identity was already documented as lane-dependent (captured_under: numpy 2.0.2 and 2.4.4 disagree in the 16th digit of exp()). A solver change moves the same digits. The numbers are still compared, through csv_contents, at the policy's rtol 1e-9, which is the tolerance that means something
full_repr_csv_bytes.numeric_strings: a csv_contents cell that is a string on both sides and parses as a finite float on both sides is compared as a number under the general rule rather than as text. Without that the CSV columns pandas leaves as object dtype (a value column holding both names and numbers) would be compared byte for byte and the 1e-9 this policy promises for csv_contents would never be applied

expected_to_move_across_platforms._what: what may differ when the suite runs anywhere but Windows, where every golden was captured: the MUPE and ZMPE statistics of the learning_curve_compare_methods block of lots_cost_core.json.gz, both the fitting.fit results and their rows of the comparison table; every fit's iteration count in that block, OLS included; and the sign of the Mean bias the two exact-fit lots fixtures print as zero, which sits outside the block. tests/golden_support.py builds OVERRIDES entries, one exclusion and the printed-zero patterns from this entry, and builds nothing from it on Windows
expected_to_move_across_platforms._why: the last bits of the arithmetic depend on the machine as well as the stack. The same numpy on the same computer draws about 0.5% of the lognormal reference model's values in tests/test_monte_carlo.py one to nine ulps apart under Windows and under Linux, numpy 2.4.4 on both, and OpenBLAS picks its kernels by CPU: forced onto its kernels without FMA (OPENBLAS_CORETYPE Sandybridge or Nehalem) under WSL it moves 82 leaves where the default kernels move 50, and three GitHub lanes moved some of the same extra leaves on their own. cost_core.learning_curve gives fitting no analytic Jacobian, so fitting takes central differences, which divide a last-bit disagreement by the step, and all three methods iterate on the result. The MUPE and ZMPE refits land about 1e-8 apart; their loops, and on some kernels the OLS loop, stop one or two steps earlier or later; the OLS numbers still agree to 1e-9 on every run that printed them. Outside this block the only leaves that move are the Mean bias cells printed_zero_sign names. No other leaf of any golden moves on any run, the lot engine's included, whose models carry analytic Jacobians. This is the sensitivity tests/goldens/README.md records for numpy and scipy upgrades, reached through the machine instead of the stack
expected_to_move_across_platforms._measured_not_guessed: on 32 Linux runs. Twelve are the GitHub Actions lanes of the tree tagged v1.0.0, from the push of main and from the push of the tag (python 3.9 to 3.14 on ubuntu; each log prints its first 40 leaves). Ten of them move the same 50 leaves, in scatter_0.1 and scatter_0.3; the 3.10 and 3.14 lanes of the tag's run move 73, twenty of them in scatter_0.05 and two of them the clean_series Mean bias signs outside the block; the rest of their 73 was not printed. Two are python 3.12 under WSL (Ubuntu 24.04, glibc 2.39) on the machine the goldens came from, uncapped, once on the pinned stack (numpy 2.4.4, pandas 3.0.3, scipy 1.17.1) and once on the 3.9 lane's floor (numpy 2.0.2, pandas 2.3.3, scipy 1.13.1): the same 50 leaves as each other, by the same amounts to one ulp on one slope_lower_80. Six are the GitHub lanes of the push after, where one runner, on the same stack as two lanes that passed, moved the OLS iteration count and ten Mean bias signs. Twelve are uncapped WSL runs on the pinned, floor and CI-resolved (numpy 2.4.6, pandas 3.0.5, scipy 1.17.1) stacks: two force nothing, and the rest switch numpy's X86_V3 dispatch off, force OpenBLAS onto its Sandybridge, Nehalem or Zen kernels, run one BLAS thread, or combine those. Two also asked numpy to drop AVX2 and FMA3: numpy 2.4.6 did not, numpy 2.0.2 on the floor run did, and it changed nothing. Only the OpenBLAS kernels without FMA change anything, and the five runs on them agree with each other to one ulp on one slope_lower_80. They move 82 leaves, 40 that the default kernels do not: nine in scatter_0.05, more of the scatter_0.1 MUPE fit, the iteration counts of all three methods and eight Mean bias signs; and 8 of the default 50 fall back inside 1e-9. Windows, python 3.14 and 3.9, moves nothing. _measured_maxima is the largest move of each field over every run that printed its values
expected_to_move_across_platforms._how_the_allowances_are_sized: by the rule expected_to_move_beyond_rtol_in_step_2 states: the smallest power of ten that clears the largest measured move by at least three times, with an absolute allowance only where a leaf sits so near zero that its relative move is arithmetic about nothing, and then, as b (learning) does in step 2, on the whole field: theta and r_squared carry theirs on every leaf. T1 1e-6 over 3.820e-8 (26x; 1e-7 would be 2.6x). slope and its two 80% bounds 1e-7 over 7.953e-9 (12.6x). fitted 1e-7 over 2.342e-8 (4.3x). theta 1e-7 over theta[0]'s 4.832e-9 (20.7x), plus an atol of 1e-7 for theta[1], the log2 of a slope near one, which is -0.012 on the scatter_0.3 ZMPE fit and moves 1.119e-8 there, 9.3e-7 relative (8.9x); _atol_on_the_exponents is the same case in step 2. cov 1e-8 over 3.181e-9 (3.1x). r_squared 1e-7 over 1.875e-8 (5.3x), plus an atol of 1e-7 for the scatter_0.3 ZMPE r_squared, which is -0.0014 and moves 1.736e-8 (5.8x). sigma, standard_error and cv, and the table's std_error and cv, which move only on the kernels without FMA, 1e-8 over 1.331e-9 (7.5x). Mean percent error, a cancelling sum of order 1e-11, atol 1e-9 over 2.374e-10 (4.2x). Apart from mean percent error, which is noise about zero whatever its figures say, every allowance sits about ten times or more below the fourth significant figure of the leaf it covers
expected_to_move_across_platforms._what_is_given_up: off Windows, a move in these leaves smaller than its allowance goes unseen, the three iteration counts are not compared at all, and the exact-fit fixtures' Mean bias cells pass whenever both sides print a zero. That includes the numpy 2.5.3 and scipy 1.18.1 moves tests/goldens/README.md records for this block. Measured under Linux with this entry in place, numpy 2.5.3 and scipy 1.18.1 each pass the whole suite, so off Windows nothing sees either of them, and a raise of the numpy or scipy cap has to be measured on Windows. On Windows nothing is given up: this entry builds nothing there, every leaf is compared at rtol 1e-9, the iteration counts exactly and the Mean bias cells as printed

n_iter.why: every fit's iteration count in this block is a loop counter, like iteration_detail, and it moves by one or two steps. Under Linux the scatter_0.3 MUPE loop takes 12 steps where it took 11 under Windows, and 13 on the kernels without FMA, which also take the scatter_0.3 OLS loop from 5 to 4, the scatter_0.3 ZMPE from 40 to 39 and the scatter_0.1 MUPE from 7 to 6. One GitHub runner moved the scatter_0.3 OLS count on its own, and the two 73-leaf lanes of the v1.0.0 tag's run, python 3.10 and 3.14, moved the scatter_0.1 ZMPE count from 34 to 36. converged, and every number each loop produces, are still compared

printed_zero_sign.why: the Mean bias of the two exact-fit lots fixtures is the mean of residuals at the floating-point floor, so it prints as a zero and its sign is the sign of a rounding error. A BLAS kernel without FMA (OPENBLAS_CORETYPE Sandybridge or Nehalem under WSL), three GitHub lanes (one that flipped ten cells both ways, and the two 73-leaf lanes of the v1.0.0 tag's run, which flipped the two clean_series LC+Rate cells among the leaves they printed), and numpy 2.5.3 all turn -0.00% into +0.00% or back. Off Windows these cells compare equal when both sides print the same zero, whatever its sign; a printed digit, or any other change in how the zero is written, still fails

_measured_maxima._note: the largest move each field makes over every Linux run that printed its values (the twelve GitHub lanes and the two WSL runs of v1.0.0, and the twelve forced-kernel runs), and where. The sigma, standard_error, std_error, cv and mean percent error maxima are the scatter_0.1 MUPE fit's, the same to the bit on all five runs forced onto an OpenBLAS kernel without FMA, Sandybridge or Nehalem, on all three stacks; the rest are on scatter_0.3, under the default kernels

fits r_squared.at: zmpe, where r_squared is -0.0014; the largest relative move away from zero is 1.875e-8, on mupe

fits n_iter.at: scatter_0.3 mupe on the kernels without FMA (12 on the default kernels); every count that moved is in not_compared_off_platform.n_iter.why

expected_to_move_across_platforms.unchanged_at_the_general_rule: everything else, on every platform: every number of the OLS fit and of the OLS row of the table, observed, df, n_obs, n_params and converged of every fit, and every other leaf of every golden bar the Mean bias cells printed_zero_sign names and the one masked path separator test_error_paths reads through neutral_separators. None of those moved on any run, among the leaves each run printed; the GitHub lanes print only their first 40

workbooks.resolution: every numeric xlsx cell is written rounded by the engine (2 dp costs, 4 dp midpoints; Risk_Summary values are formatted strings), so compare_workbooks.py --rtol 1e-9 has an effective resolution of about 0.005/|value|. The JSON goldens (ctx, midpoints.forecast_unrounded, enrich, derived_stats) are the only 1e-9 authority; the workbook check guards layout, sheet/chart structure and the rounded values
workbooks.wbs_<program>.xlsx: risk variant: Program_SCurve, Program_Tornado and the risk rows/columns of Program_Summary and Program_Elements change in step 3; regress wbs_<program>_plain.xlsx and wbs_<program>_plain_nosens.xlsx instead (compare_workbooks.py --skip-sheets Program_SCurve,Program_Tornado for the risk one)
workbooks.engine_<case>_app_risk.xlsx: risk sheets are seeded (n_iter 20000, seed 11, rho 0.30; the GUI defaults); tests/test_workbook.py:48-50 writes n_iter 4000 seed 11 instead: that is engine_app_example_app_risk_n4000.xlsx

wbs_program_workbook_sensitivity: wbs_<program>.xlsx and _plain.xlsx carry Buy_Sensitivity from buy_profile_sensitivity; the GUI passes sensitivity_result=None unless the analyst ran it first (lot_cost_model.py:3134-3136): that is _plain_nosens.xlsx

compare_workbooks_py.ignored_rows: cells whose value, row label or column header matches: run timestamp, tool version, 'Generated ...', saved_at, git rev/revision, and 'Enriched by' (Risk_Summary B2 is the static 'cost_core (cost-risk-toolkit)' today, risk.py:274; ignored so a 1.0.0 version stamp in that row does not fail the workbook check)
compare_workbooks_py.charts: --charts compares, per workbook, the chart count, the one-cell anchors (col,row) of every drawing, and per chart the series count, axis <delete val> flags and dLbls count; the regexes are namespace-agnostic because openpyxl 3.1.5 writes chart/drawing parts in the default namespace without c:/xdr: prefixes. compare_workbooks.py --selftest checks the signature is live (engine_*_app_risk.xlsx: 5 charts, 5 anchors, series > 0); check_determinism.py runs that self-test on every workbook with the expected chart count
